final_message:
I fixed `transpose` in `src/matrix.py`. I haven't run it or any tests.

The old version used the row count as the size for both dimensions, so it only worked on square matrices. A non-square input like 2×3 either dropped columns or raised an `IndexError`. It now builds one output row per column of the input, so rectangular matrices work.

An empty matrix returns `[]`. A matrix whose rows are all empty (such as `[[]]`) also returns `[]`.
